newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan rivals clash on northern plains.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rivals clash on northern plains.

text.p: Rival Afghan militia battled for control of plains north of Kabul on Tuesday, but the capital's fortnight-old Taleban rulers dismissed recent military reverses and vowed a "tooth-breaking response".

Forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood have rolled back last month's advance by the Taleban as far as the town of Qara Bagh, a 30-minute drive from Kabul, Reuter correspondent Kurt Schork reported from the town.

But in a twist characteristic of Afghanistan's long-running civil war, Taleban fighters re-entered the town under cover of Monday night and by Tuesday were flying their trademark white flag above the marketplace.

"Now our mujahideen (holy warriors) are well-organised, well-prepared and if the enemy tries to attack they will receive a tooth-breaking response from our mujahideen," acting Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said in Kabul.

The purist Taleban, born in the refugee camps along the Afghan-Pakistan border two years ago, has faced its first serious reverses in the past week as guerrilla mastermind Masood swept from his valley stronghold two hours' north of Kabul.

Sealing two pacts with fellow northern militia leader Abdul Rashid Dostum -- an Uzbek commander and once a rival -- and with other regional leaders Masood has pushed south through the towns of Jabal os-Siraj and Charikar towards Kabul.

Neither side has reported casualties in this latest bout of fighting across the plain, but Taleban sources contacted from the Pakistan capital of Islamabad said more than 200 Taleban wounded have been ferried to the southern town of Kandahar.

Mullah Abdul Razzak, a member of the Taleban's ruling six-man interim shura (council) had been lightly wounded, the sources said, although Mutaqi denied reports he had been captured, saying he was shuttling between Kabul and the front.

More ominous for the Taleban has been Monday's agreement between Dostum, Masood and other regional leaders in which Dostum agreed to recognise the deposed government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, Masood's political mentor.

It was not immediately clear whether Dostum would throw his military weight behind any attempt by Masood to regain the capital. Without it, Afghan watchers said, Masood would find it almost impossible to dislodge the Taleban.

The Taleban's Mutaqi dismissed the alliance, although he reiterated the movement's readiness to talk to Dostum. The Taleban have been keen to avoid fighting both at the same time, and have stressed they have no problem with Dostum.
"In the face of any alliance we keep our previous position," he told a news conference in Kabul.

"In the case of the (Masood) militia that ran away from Kabul, if they submit or hand over the government's property we have no problem with them, and as for the northern forces (of Dostum) we are ready to talk to them," he said.
A high-ranking Pakistan delegation, including Interior Minister Nazeerullah Babar, was in Kabul on Tuesday, apparently as part of efforts by Afghanistan's neighbour to help broker a peace deal.
Afghan watchers said they believed Babar had gone on to Kandahar, the Taleban headquarters, possibly to see the movement's founder, Mullah Mohammed Omar.
There was no confirmation of the report.
Pakistan has supported the Taleban but has denied supplying military aid.
On the plains north of Kabul, Taleban forces harried attempts by Masood to consolidate and expand his gains.

An unknown aircraft presumably flying in support of Taleban forces bombed Jabal os-Siraj on Tuesday, mirroring a similar attack on Charikar to the south a day earlier in which nine people were killed.

More fighting was heard near the military airbase of Bagram, 50 km (30 miles) north of the capital where Masood forces claimed they had taken all but a corner of the strategic airfield. The Taleban denied it had fallen.

"I have heard this rumour on the radio but I can tell you that our mujahideen are still based aronnd the Bagram airbase and have not withdrawn. Those who have launched this news either are ignorant or are snakes," Mutaqi said.
